representative_server: llama.cpp llama-server (native /completion and /v1/chat/completions with llama.cpp extensions)
note: Representative payloads for modelrack.providers.llamacpp's conformance and unit tests, not captures: the machine this phase was written on has no llama.cpp build, so nothing here came off a running server (spec §19). Each body was written to the server's own serialization code at build b10792 — tools/server/server-task.cpp (to_json_non_oaicompat, to_json_oaicompat_chat, to_json_oaicompat_chat_stream, usage_json_oaicompat), server-common.cpp (server_slot_stats::to_json, format_error_response, format_oai_sse) and server-context.cpp (send_final_response, send_error, the /props and /health handlers) — fetched and read on the date above, rather than to the README alone. tests/live/test_llamacpp_live.py is what proves these shapes against a real server; until it has been run the fixtures represent the documented and read behaviour, not observed behaviour.

what_each_proves.completion*.json: Native /completion: tokens_evaluated is the prompt total, tokens_predicted the output, timings.cache_n the cached prefix. tokens_cached is carried at its real value — the slot's whole cache, prompt + output (33 for 21 + 12) — so an adapter that started reading it as cached input fails the reconciliation arithmetic. completion_cached.json: cache_n 8 of 21 → input 13. completion_no_cache_n.json: a build predating cache_n → cache classes 0, input the whole prompt. completion_no_timings.json: counts without timings → the same. completion_no_counts.json: this shape's absent usage object → every class UNSUPPORTED. completion_limit.json: stop_type limit → LENGTH.
what_each_proves.chat_complete*.json: The chat shape as llama-server writes it: usage with prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens from the same server-side counter as timings.cache_n, a timings object, and system_fingerprint carrying the build. chat_complete_cached.json is the conformance CACHE_DETAIL case (21 prompt, 8 cached → 13 input); chat_complete_no_usage.json the NO_USAGE_OBJECT case; chat_complete_details_unreadable.json a details object the adapter must refuse rather than guess; chat_complete_reasoning.json reasoning_content; chat_complete_tool_calls.json a parsed tool call.
what_each_proves.chat_stream*.sse: The chat stream: data: events, a finish chunk, then — because the adapter sends stream_options.include_usage — a usage chunk with an empty choices array carrying usage and timings, then data: [DONE]. chat_stream_no_usage.sse is a server that sent no usage chunk (every class UNSUPPORTED); chat_stream_truncated.sse ends without [DONE]; chat_stream_error.sse carries a mid-stream data: {"error": …} event, which is how format_oai_sse writes an error.
what_each_proves.completion_stream*.sse: The native stream: one data: event per token with stop false, then the final result with stop true, content empty (send_final_response clears it in stream mode), and the full timings. No [DONE] is ever sent on this endpoint — the stop chunk is the terminal rule.
what_each_proves.error_*.json: format_error_response's {error: {code, message, type}}; error_context_overflow.json adds the n_prompt_tokens and n_ctx fields server_task_result_error::to_json appends for exceed_context_size_error, which is what lets ContextLimitExceeded carry real numbers here.
what_each_proves.health_*.json, props*.json: GET /health's two answers, and GET /props with build_info and default_generation_settings.n_ctx — the reported served context.
what_each_proves.lora_adapters.json: GET /lora-adapters as server_task_result_get_lora::to_json writes it at build b10792 (tools/server/server-task.cpp): a JSON *array* of {id, path, scale, task_name, prompt_prefix}, where id is the index in the order --lora was given and scale is the launch scale — 1.0, because --lora-init-without-apply governs only whether the set is applied to the context at init and does not zero it. That last fact is why the adapter always sends a complete lora field rather than relying on the server's default: launch_slot_with_task restores params_base.lora_adapters when a request carries none, and takes that branch without consulting lora_should_clear_cache.
